name: Rewiring America (charityevals)
beneficiaries_note: Our build: a tonne of greenhouse gas kept out of the air spares people everywhere, so the result is spread by world population; the small US smoke share is left in the world figure.
summary: Rewiring America works to electrify American homes: it designed the Inflation Reduction Act's home-electrification rebates and runs free tools and coaching that help households switch to heat pumps and other electric appliances (.7M spent in 2024, its first year filing on its own after leaving the Windward Fund). This model counts its share of the law's home-energy provisions (rebates and home credits) won in 2021-2024 and the households its tools and coaches bring to switch sooner, against a typical year's spending in that period. At the defaults a dollar given averts about 0.004 tonnes of CO₂e (about  a tonne), 0.0009 years of healthy life per ,000, about 95% of it from the law; it is low because the home provisions are a small part of the law's tonnes, the law's credit is shared with many groups and with what governments would have done anyway, and the 2025 budget law ended the home credits after 2025. The result is mostly uncertainty: its own ranges alone span about a thousandfold, the biggest being the discount rate, the shared years a won reform counts and the home provisions' share of the law; both branches are discounted for missing data, since no tonne is measured for its work.

rows.explainer: The period starts in 2021, the year of the Build Back Better bill whose climate provisions, Rewiring America's rebate plan among them, became the Inflation Reduction Act in August 2022 (Rewiring America was founded in 2020), and ends with its latest accounts (2024): four years, the law and the first two years of its consumer tools and the states' rebate programmes.

rows.label: Years in the period
Average yearly spending 2021-2024, in 2024 prices, ÷ 2024's reported cost
rows.explainer: A past average's cost and wins come from the same period (templates.md Convention 11), but 2021 to mid-2024 sit inside the Windward Fund's accounts, which don't report its projects separately: a ranged judgment anchored on the nearest year. 2024's return ($22.7M) holds the second half-year's operations (about $15M after the affiliate's repayments) plus the $7.4M settlement for earlier costs, so a full 2024 was probably $25-35M; 2023, with the law's rollout and 122 staff by 2024, was likely similar; 2021 and 2022, a start-up founded in 2020, much smaller. The average year is about 0.9 of the reported cost (0.5 to 1.5).

rows.label: Cost of a typical year of the period, with overhead
Share of the Inflation Reduction Act's projected 2030 cut from its home-energy provisions

source.title: Canary Media (2022), Climate bill could spur market transformation in home electrification (16 August 2022)
source.quote: Based on a Rewiring America plan

rows.explainer: The provisions Rewiring America worked on: the $4.5B electrification rebates (HEEHRA, now HEAR), the $4.3B efficiency rebates (HOMES) and the larger home-improvement and home clean-energy credits (25C, 25D). Rewiring America forecast that the rebates could help about 1 million households go all-electric (Canary Media), about 3 million tonnes a year at the shared per-home figure; the credits' heat pumps and rooftop solar add perhaps 10-20 million tonnes a year by 2030. Against the law's projected 900 million (facts: climate.ira_tco2e_per_year_2030), about 2.5% (1% to 6%), our judgment; buildings are a small part of every model's projection, which is mostly power and vehicles.

rows.label: Inflation Reduction Act's home-energy provisions: tonnes of CO₂e a year they would cut by 2030
rows.explainer: The shared projection of the law's whole cut (facts: climate.ira_tco2e_per_year_2030), the same figure the Union of Concerned Scientists' and the Environmental Defense Fund's models start from, times the home-energy provisions' share.

rows.label: Households using its digital tools, 2024

source.title: Rewiring America, Inc., Form 990 for calendar year 2024 (IRS e-file, object 932830316_202412)
source.quote: DIGITAL TOOLS LEVERAGED BY OVER 200,000 HOUSEHOLD USERS

rows.explainer: The incentive calculator, the personal electrification planner and the savings tool, as the return counts them for 2024 (its own count, together with its affiliate). Partners' sites that embed its incentives data (Efficiency Vermont's calculator, for one) aren't in it.

rows.label: Average yearly tool users 2021-2024 ÷ 2024's
rows.explainer: The calculator launched in September 2022, so 2021 and most of 2022 had none, while 2023, the law's first full year, drew heavy use (a 2024 Rewiring America presentation reported some 700,000 calculations since launch, which we could not open ourselves). Spread over the period's four years, about 0.8 of 2024's count a year (0.4 to 1.3), our judgment.

rows.label: Share of tool users who electrify sooner because of the tools (a heat pump's worth)
rows.explainer: Of the households who use the calculator or planner, how many make a switch worth a heat pump's tonnes (a heat pump, or a heat-pump water heater, induction stove and the like adding up to one) sooner than they would have without them. No one has measured it: the users are mostly already interested, and information alone moves few home-energy decisions (free energy audits and home energy reports change only a few per cent of households' behaviour in the randomised trials). 1.5% (0.3% to 5%), our judgment; the years sooner are a row below.

rows.label: Electrification coaches trained, 2024

source.title: Rewiring America, Inc., Form 990 for calendar year 2024 (IRS e-file, object 932830316_202412)

rows.explainer: Its Coaches programme: a free four-week course on upgrading a home, after which coaches help neighbours in peer groups.

rows.label: Switches per coach trained (a heat pump's worth, sooner because of the course)
rows.explainer: A coach is a volunteer who chose a four-week course on electrifying homes: more likely than a tool user to switch, and to bring a neighbour along. 0.25 switches per coach (0.1 to 0.5), our judgment.

rows.label: Households switching sooner because of the tools and coaching, per year of the period
Refrigerant leaks of a heat pump, tonnes of CO₂e a year

source.title: Canary Media (2024), Yes, heat pumps slash emissions, even if powered by a dirty grid (11 March 2024), reporting Wilson et al. (2024), Joule
source.quote: Typical leakage rates of R-410A increase emissions on average by only 0.07 metric tons of CO2 equivalent per year

rows.explainer: A side effect, small: the refrigerant a heat pump leaks warms the climate too. Taken off the per-home cut, which counts only energy.

rows.label: Tonnes of CO₂e a year one home cuts by switching, refrigerant taken off
rows.explainer: The shared per-home cut of a heat pump (facts: climate.us_heat_pump_tco2e_per_household_year, NREL's simulation of the US housing stock: 2.5 to 4.4 tonnes a year, the extra power's emissions counted), less the refrigerant leaks.

rows.label: Tools and coaching: tonnes of CO₂e a year cut by the households who switch in a year
Share of the law's home-energy provisions due to advocacy at all
rows.explainer: The law is in: what's uncertain is how much of a won policy advocacy caused rather than the government's agenda, events and opinion. The shared share for every climate model (facts: climate.advocacy_share_of_policy_win, 30%), split among all advocates by the attribution row.

rows.label: Years a won reform counts before it would have come anyway
rows.explainer: The site's one answer (docs/normalization.md 2.9).

rows.label: Years from the law until its home-energy tonnes are avoided
rows.explainer: The shared wait for rules and tax credits (facts: climate.years_until_avoided_regulation, 3 years): the credits paid from 2023, while the states' rebate programmes opened only from late 2024.

rows.label: The law's wait, discounted
rows.explainer: The wait discounted at the shared rate; the unit's conversion then discounts the heat deaths from the year the tonne is avoided, so nothing is discounted twice.

rows.label: Discounted years the law's tonnes count
Inflation Reduction Act's home-energy provisions: tonnes due to all advocacy over the years counted
The law's tonnes due to advocacy, per year of the period
rows.explainer: One win in the period's four years, spread over them like the costs (Convention 11).

rows.label: Years sooner a household switches because of the tools
rows.explainer: A switch made sooner counts only until the household would have switched anyway, at its next replacement or as gas gets dearer and heat pumps cheaper. A furnace lasts 15-20 years and a heat pump about 15, so a switch made at a breakdown that would otherwise have gone back to gas is brought forward by up to a heat pump's life; one a few years ahead of plan by less. 7 years (3 to 15), our judgment.

rows.label: Years from using the tools until the switch is installed
rows.explainer: Planning, quotes and installation: a few months to a year or more. Half a year (a quarter to a year and a half), our judgment.

rows.label: Discounted years a tool-led switch counts
Tools and coaching: tonnes of CO₂e over the years counted, per year of the period
Tonnes before adjustments, per year of the period
Evidence adjustment: how far the projected and simulated tonnes should be trusted
rows.explainer: The law's tonnes are a modeller's projection and the per-home cut a simulation, not measured cuts; projections of tax credits have run ahead of what was built, and homes that switch with a tool's help may not be the stock's average. 0.8 (0.5 to 1.1), our judgment, as the Union of Concerned Scientists' and the Environmental Defense Fund's models for the same kinds of estimate.

rows.label: Inflation Reduction Act: share of its tonnes that wouldn't have happened anyway
rows.explainer: The shared figure for the law (facts: climate.ira_counterfactual, 80%), as every model counting it uses.

rows.label: Inflation Reduction Act's home-energy provisions: Rewiring America's share of the advocacy behind them

source.title: Canary Media (2022), Climate bill could spur market transformation in home electrification (16 August 2022)
source.quote: Based on a Rewiring America plan

rows.explainer: The electrification rebates were built on Rewiring America's own plan (Canary Media), and it was the leading voice for paying households to switch appliances; the efficiency rebates and the credits had long-standing backers (efficiency and solar groups, NRDC, the Building Decarbonization Coalition, manufacturers), and the whole law many more. 25% (10% to 50%), our judgment. Over the whole law that is 2.5% × 25%, about 0.6%, beside 1% for the Union of Concerned Scientists and 2% for the Environmental Defense Fund, both larger groups working across the law.

rows.label: Inflation Reduction Act's home-energy provisions: credit share used
rows.explainer: The charity's share of the resources behind the outcome; it applies whichever way credit is shared.

rows.label: Home-energy provisions' delivered share relative to the whole law's

source.title: US Internal Revenue Service (2025), FAQs for modification of sections 25C, 25D, 25E, 30C, 30D, 45L, 45W and 179D under Public Law 119-21 (the One, Big, Beautiful Bill)
source.note: The 2025 budget law ends the 25C credit for property placed in service after 31 December 2025, and 25D on the same date.

rows.explainer: The 2025 budget law ended both home credits after 2025, ten years early, while the $8.8B of rebates were left funded and the states kept opening programmes, slowly. The whole law kept less (its power credits end for projects begun after 2027), so the home provisions kept somewhat less than the law's own delivered share or about as much: 0.8 (0.4 to 1.2) of it, our judgment.

rows.label: Inflation Reduction Act's home-energy provisions: share of their tonnes delivered
rows.explainer: The shared delivered share of the law (facts: climate.ira_delivered_share, 35%) times the home provisions' relative row: about 28%.

rows.label: Tools and coaching: share of their switches not already in the law's projected tonnes
rows.explainer: The years sooner already say what the households would have done without the tools. What remains is overlap with the law's branch: its projection assumes households take up its credits and rebates, and a tool that helps a household claim them partly delivers that projected uptake, counted there at Rewiring America's share. 80% (60% to 100%), our judgment.

rows.label: Tools and coaching: Rewiring America's share of the resources behind the switches
rows.explainer: A switch the tools brought sooner also took a contractor's quote and sales effort, the rebate and utility programmes' outreach and, for coaches, their own volunteer time. 50% (20% to 80%), our judgment.

rows.label: Tools and coaching: credit share used
rows.explainer: The charity's share of the resources behind the outcome; it applies whichever way credit is shared.

rows.label: Counted less where the outcome isn't measured for this charity
rows.explainer: The shared missing-data step (docs/normalization.md 2.12): no tonne is measured for Rewiring America's work; the law's tonnes are a projection, its part a judgment, and how many tool users switch because of the tools is unmeasured. Both branches take it.

rows.label: Inflation Reduction Act branch: all adjustments
Tools and coaching branch: all adjustments
Share that wouldn't have happened anyway (outcome-weighted average of the branches, for reading only)
Rewiring America's share of the resources (outcome-weighted average of the branches, for reading only)

rows.label: Credit share used (outcome-weighted average of the branches, for reading only)
All adjustments (outcome-weighted average of the branches, for reading only)
Other work not modelled, as a share of the modelled value

source.title: Rewiring America (2025), A letter from our CEO (8 May 2025)
source.quote: negotiated with manufacturers to lower the cost of heat pumps for households by 40 percent

rows.explainer: The rest of the work, each a share of the modelled value: heat-pump prices it negotiated with manufacturers for its programmes and a free database of 3,500 incentives that utilities and states build on, which may speed switches beyond its own users, 10%; free technical analyses for states and cities applying for funds and for utility programmes and rates, and its research (the health and jobs reports), 7%; community demonstration projects in five places, 3%. 20% (5% to 50%), our judgment. Lower bills for most households that switch (Wilson et al. 2024 find 62-95% save) are left out: a few hundred dollars a year to a US household is very little on the site's scale.

rows.label: Side effect: cleaner indoor air where a gas stove is replaced, as a share of the modelled value

source.title: Gruenwald, Seals, Knibbs & Hosgood (2022), Population attributable fraction of gas stoves and childhood asthma in the United States, International Journal of Environmental Research and Public Health 20(1): 75
source.quote: We found that 12.7% (95% CI = 6.3−19.3%) of current childhood asthma in the US is attributable to gas stove use.
source.note: Abstract, read through Europe PMC. Contested: Cox (2023, Global Epidemiology) argues the meta-analysed odds ratios do not support a causal share.

rows.explainer: Some switches replace a gas stove with induction, and gas stoves are linked to childhood asthma: Gruenwald et al. attribute 12.7% of US childhood asthma to them, from meta-analysed observational odds ratios (contested as causal evidence: Cox 2023). Per stove replaced in a home with children that is worth about as much as the climate value of a heat pump's tonnes over the same years, but stoves are a small part of the switches counted, which are mostly heating. 5% (0 to 20%) of the modelled value, our judgment.

rows.label: Share of these tonnes that are methane
rows.explainer: Gas a home stops burning also stops leaking upstream (facts: climate.us_home_electrification_methane_share, 10%): both branches' tonnes come from homes electrified. The shared conversion values it by methane's own, earlier warming and ozone.

rows.label: Share of these tonnes from burning less fossil fuel near people
rows.explainer: Every tonne here except the upstream methane is gas, oil or propane no longer burned in homes, net of the extra power plants' fuel.

rows.label: Smoke per tonne of these cuts, relative to the fossil-fuel average
rows.explainer: The shared factor for tonnes from US homes electrified (facts: climate.us_home_electrification_smoke_factor, 0.02): gas no longer burned at ground level near people, less the extra power plants' mostly scrubbed smoke. The law's branch also holds some rooftop solar (25D), whose smoke is US power's (0.013, inside the range).

rows.label: Air pollution these tonnes cut, relative to an average fossil-fuel tonne
rows.explainer: Read by the tco2e unit's conversion (docs/normalization.md 2.5).

rows.label: Air-pollution deaths averted per tonne, counted directly (none here)
rows.explainer: No source counts deaths beside these tonnes; their smoke is in air_pollution_weight, so nothing is counted twice.

rows.label: Tonnes of CO₂e averted per year of the period
rows.explainer: Each branch's tonnes × its own adjustments, summed, with the other work and the indoor-air side effect added as shares.
